Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

physical adjective

of the body

also physically, bodily, physical exercise, physical pain, physical strength, physical health

classical

Cic. Cael. 39: in labōre corporis atque in animī contentiōne
Cic. Sen. 36

corporis

genitive of corpus, after its noun

of the body

Latin says “of the body”: physical strength is vīrēs corporis, physical pain dolor corporis, physical exercise exercitātiō corporis or simply exercitātiō (see exercise). Against the mind it is corpus and animus: corpore senex, old in body (Cic. Sen. 38).

Other words

  • corporeus, corporea, corporeum — of the body; made of flesh

    also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.41: ignis corporeus, the body’s heat (Lewis & Short)

    Rare in prose (Lewis & Short: chiefly Lucretius); its usual sense is material, having a body (see physical, material).

  • corporālis, corporāle — bodily, of the body

    also used · post-classical · Sen. Ep. 78.22: voluptātēs corporālēs (Lewis & Short)

    Post-Augustan, most often in the jurists (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nec vērō corporī sōlum subveniendum est, sed mentī atque animō multō magis

    and it is not only the body that needs help, but the mind and spirit much moreCic. Sen. 36

  • omnemque vītae suae cursum in labōre corporis atque in animī contentiōne cōnficeret

    and spent his whole life in physical toil and mental effortCic. Cael. 39

See also physical, body, exercise, health, mind.

SourcesLewis & Short: corpus · Lewis & Short: corporeus · Lewis & Short: corporalis
